channel.title: linux-cleanup release notes
channel.description: Every linux-cleanup release, command line and desktop app.

item.title: Desktop 1.0.3
item.description: Ships with the command line 2.1.1 and current libraries.
item.content:encoded: The app now ships with the command line 2.1.1 and current libraries. Nothing changed in what it cleans. The app updates itself.

item.title: CLI 2.1.1
item.description: The help, version and About screens point to the website, this manual and the desktop download.
item.content:encoded: --help, --version and the menu's About box now point to the website, this manual and the desktop app's download page. The About box also says plainly that the script reads the public release record once at start. Nothing changed in what any mode removes. Run it with npx -y linux-cleanup@2.1.1 --version.

item.title: Desktop 1.0.2
item.description: Clearer wording on the Updates screen and a working check command on the errors screen.
item.content:encoded: Clearer wording on the Updates screen, and the errors screen now copies a command that works: npx -y linux-cleanup --self-test. The app updates itself.

item.title: Desktop 1.0.1
item.description: Error reports with no paths or file names, a walkthrough with real screens, a Get linux-cleanup page and steadier page tours.
item.content:encoded:
Error reports reach us without paths or file names, the walkthrough shows real screens, and Help has a Get linux-cleanup page listing every place it runs.

Page tours keep each step in view as you move through them. The app updated itself from 1.0.0. See installing the desktop app.

item.title: Desktop 1.0.0
item.description: The first desktop release, an AppImage and .deb for x86_64 Linux bundling CLI 2.1.0.
item.content:encoded:
The first desktop release: the all-safe cleanup in a window, with a dry run before every real run and a receipt after it.

AppImage and .deb for x86_64 Linux, bundling CLI 2.1.0. It updates itself from signed releases. Start with installing the desktop app.

item.title: CLI 2.1.0
item.description: --json-events streams local, versioned JSON events for --scan and non-interactive all-safe runs, dry runs included.
item.content:encoded:
--json-events streams local, versioned JSON events for --scan and non-interactive --all-safe --yes.

Adding --dry-run to all-safe reports proposed paths without deleting them. The stream can contain full local paths, so keep it on the machine. The JSON events reference and the changelog have the details.

item.title: CLI 2.0.1
item.description: The README lists every place linux-cleanup is released. No change to what the script does.
item.content:encoded: The README lists every place linux-cleanup is released. No change to what the script does.

item.title: CLI 2.0.0
item.description: linux-cleanup 2.0.0 adds --dry-run, a release-record check on start and --refresh-app.
item.content:encoded:
Added --dry-run, a public release-record check on start, and --refresh-app for the persistent CLI copy.

Normal release notices allow the first run and block from the next start; urgent notices block an older copy at once. Offline runs continue. A dry run does not remove cleanup targets or change settings, though it may write a local log and update-check state. Read the changelog for the full entry.
